title: The Casualties Are Counted and Charat Singh’s Valor Is Remembered

blocks.text: As the guarded withdrawal continues, wounded and separated Singhs slowly rejoin the caravan while news arrives that many others died or got scattered from the caravan. The page lingers on the scale of the disaster, showing how survival itself is uncertain from one mile to the next.

The chronicler then turns from confusion to testimony and says that the author records the number his eyewitness father told, preserving memory through family witness when exact counting has become nearly impossible. This makes the page both historical and mournful, because it acknowledges that even remembered numbers can only approximate such devastation.

Within that grief, Charat Singh emerges as the figure most widely praised for steadiness, rescue, and personal daring. His name becomes attached not just to bravery in combat but to the many lives of Sikhs in the caravan that he helped save during the Ghallughara.
